[In this question, the perpendicular unit vectors $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are in a horizontal plane.]
In this question you must show all stages of your working.
Solutions relying on calculator technology are not acceptable.
A particle $P$ is moving on a smooth horizontal plane.
At time $t$ seconds $(t \geqslant 0)$, the position vector of $P$, relative to a fixed point $O$, is $\mathbf{r}$ metres and the velocity of $P$ is $\mathbf{v}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ where
$\mathbf{v} = (4t^2-5t)\mathbf{i}+(-10t-12)\mathbf{j}$
When $t=0$, $\mathbf{r}=2\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j}$

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Use of $\mathbf{r}=\int \mathbf{v}\,dt$. Powers going up by 1. Allow one slip in the powers
A1: $\mathbf{r}=\left(\frac{4}{3}t^3-\frac{5}{2}t^2+A\right)\mathbf{i}+(-5t^2-12t+B)\mathbf{j}$. Allow without constant of integration
M1: Use $t=2$ and $\mathbf{r}=2\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j}$ when $t=0$: $\mathbf{r}=\left(\frac{4}{3}\times 8-\frac{5}{2}\times 4+2\right)\mathbf{i}+(-5\times 4-12\times 2+6)\mathbf{j}$. Correct use of given value to obtain $\mathbf{r}$
A1: $=\frac{8}{3}\mathbf{i}-38\mathbf{j}$. Correct answer only. Allow 2.7 or better. ISW if they go on to find the magnitude.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Accept column vectors throughout

parts.label: b
parts.text:
When $t=T$ particle $P$ is moving in the direction of the vector $\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}$
(b) Find the value of $T$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $\mathbf{v}$ in direction of $\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}$. Use velocity and direction to form an equation in $T$. Condone if they have $(-)2$ on the wrong side of their equation
A1: $\Rightarrow -2(4T^2-5T)=(-10T-12)$ ($8T^2-20T-12=0$). Correct unsimplified equation in $T$ (or $t$) only
A1: $\Rightarrow T=3$. Only. Allow $t=3$.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the exact magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ when $t=2.5$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Use of $\mathbf{a}=\frac{d\mathbf{v}}{dt}$ ($\mathbf{a}=(8t-5)\mathbf{i}-10\mathbf{j}$). Powers going down by 1. Allow one slip in the powers
M1: Use of Pythagoras and $t=2.5$. Correct use of their derivative to obtain acceleration
A1: $|\mathbf{a}|=\sqrt{(20-5)^2+10^2}=\sqrt{325}=(5\sqrt{13})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. Any equivalent simplified exact form. Ignore decimals after exact answer seen.

questions.stem:
Figure 2
A uniform beam $AB$, of mass 15 kg and length 6 m, rests with end $A$ on rough horizontal ground. The end $B$ of the beam rests against a rough vertical wall.
The beam is inclined at $75^\circ$ to the ground, as shown in Figure 2.
The coefficient of friction between the beam and the wall is 0.2
The coefficient of friction between the beam and the ground is $\mu$
The beam is modelled as a uniform rod which lies in a vertical plane perpendicular to the wall.
The beam rests in limiting equilibrium.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the magnitude of the normal reaction between the beam and the wall at $B$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Moments about $A$: Dimensionally correct. Include all relevant terms. Condone sign error(s) and sin/cos confusion.
A1: $15g \times 3\cos 75^\circ = F_B \times 6\cos 75^\circ + R_B \times 6\sin 75^\circ$. Unsimplified equation with at most one error
A1: Correct unsimplified equation
M1: Use of $F_B=0.2R_B$ in their attempt at the moments equation. Seen in part (a), not just on the diagram.
A1: $R_B=19$(N) or $R_B=18.7$(N). 2 sf or 3 sf. Ignore if go on to find the total force at $A$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1: $15g \times 3\cos 75^\circ = R_B \times 1.2\cos 75^\circ + R_B \times 6\sin 75^\circ$

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
They need to form 2 equations. Mark them in the order seen. M1A1 for each correct equation
M1: Resolve horizontally: First equation. Include all relevant terms. Dimensionally correct. Condone sign error(s) and sin/cos confusion
A1: $F_A=R_B (=18.6925....)$. Correct unsimplified equation
M1: Resolve vertically: Second equation. Include all relevant terms. Dimensionally correct. Condone sign error(s) and sin/cos confusion
A1: $R_A+F_B=15g$ ($R_A=143.26...$). Correct unsimplified equation
(M1A1 for alternatives e.g. moments about $B$: $15g\times 3\cos 75^\circ = R_A\times 6\cos 75^\circ - F_A\times 6\sin 75^\circ$)
DM1: Use $F_A=\mu R_A$ to solve for $\mu$. Dependent on the 2 preceding M marks
A1: $\mu=0.13$ or better. $g$ cancels (0.1304784...)
